- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (especially >75% above 30d mean); apply smoothing filter to dampen overshoots.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative after a spike, model fails to adjust downward; force downward correction by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10d average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment volatility >0.3 in 3 consecutive days triggers lag correction: delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude.
- If sentiment is flat (0.2–0.4) and price is trending, model often misses mean reversion; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- For 30d horizon, model underestimates when sentiment is weakly positive (0.3–0.6) and price is falling; add 1–3% upward bias to counteract downward drift.
